source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Excellent nutritional status with adequate protein intake and no other identifiable pressure injury risk factors present","B":"Ability to independently reposition every couple of hours without requiring staff assistance or reminders","C":"Full mobility with an independent repositioning ability and no reported sensory or nutritional impairment","D":"Immobility, impaired sensory perception, poor nutrition, and excessive moisture (such as from incontinence)"}}
source_row.rationale: Key risk factors for pressure injury development include immobility (inability to independently reposition), impaired sensory perception (reduced ability to feel and respond to pressure/discomfort), poor nutritional status, and excessive moisture (such as from incontinence), all of which are assessed as part of tools like the Braden Scale to guide individualized prevention strategies.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ Pressure Injury Prevention, Braden risk dimensions: sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, friction/shear; accessed 2026-08-14.
